objects.description: Enumeration of supported Bech32 encodings. Values indicate no/failed decoding, legacy Bech32, or Bech32m. Used by bech32_encode and returned by bech32_decode to indicate the encoding variant. Destruction is trivial; it is a plain enum type.

functions.name: segwit_addr_encode
functions.signature: int segwit_addr_encode(char *output, const char *hrp, int ver, const uint8_t *prog, size_t prog_len);
functions.description: Encode a SegWit address into Bech32/Bech32m format. Writes a null-terminated address string for the given human-readable part (hrp), witness program version, and witness program bytes into the provided output buffer. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure. Intended for constructing network-specific SegWit addresses.
requirements: output must point to a writable buffer of size at least 73 + strlen(hrp) bytes to hold the null-terminated result (explicit).
hrp must be a valid, null-terminated human-readable part string (explicit).
ver must be between 0 and 16 inclusive (explicit).
prog must point to the witness program bytes, and prog_len specifies its length (explicit).
prog_len must be between 2 and 40 bytes inclusive (explicit).
Caller must check the return value and only use the output if the function returns 1 (explicit).

functions.name: segwit_addr_decode
functions.signature: int segwit_addr_decode(int *ver, uint8_t *prog, size_t *prog_len, const char *hrp, const char *addr);
functions.description: Decode a SegWit address string. Parses the provided null-terminated address and, if it matches the expected hrp, outputs the witness program version, bytes, and length. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure. Typically used to validate and extract the witness program from a SegWit address.
requirements: ver must point to an int that can be updated with the witness program version (explicit).
prog must point to a writable buffer of size at least 40 bytes to receive the witness program (explicit).
prog_len must point to a size_t to be updated with the number of bytes written into prog (explicit).
hrp must be the expected, null-terminated human-readable part for the target network (explicit).
addr must be a null-terminated address string to decode (explicit).
On success, the version is between 0 and 16 inclusive (explicit).
Caller must check the return value and only consume outputs if the function returns 1 (explicit).
The decoded witness program length is expected to be between 2 and 40 bytes for SegWit usage (inferred from SegWit program constraints).

functions.name: bech32_encode
functions.signature: int bech32_encode(char *output, const char *hrp, const uint8_t *data, size_t data_len, size_t max_output_len, bech32_encoding enc);
functions.description: Encode a Bech32 or Bech32m string from an HRP and an array of 5-bit data values. Writes a null-terminated Bech32/Bech32m string to output and returns 1 on success, 0 on failure. Use this for general Bech32-family encodings, including SegWit payloads after 5-bit conversion.
requirements: output must point to a writable buffer of size at least strlen(hrp) + data_len + 8 bytes to hold the null-terminated result (explicit).
hrp must be a valid, null-terminated human-readable part (explicit).
data must point to an array of 5-bit values (each value in the range 0..31) (explicit about 5-bit; range implied by 5-bit).
data_len specifies the number of entries in data (explicit).
max_output_len specifies the maximum valid length of output; for SegWit usage this maximum is 90 (explicit).
enc must be a valid bech32_encoding, either BECH32_ENCODING_BECH32 or BECH32_ENCODING_BECH32M (explicit).
Caller must check the return value and only use the output if the function returns 1 (explicit).

functions.name: bech32_decode
functions.signature: bech32_encoding bech32_decode(char *hrp, uint8_t *data, size_t *data_len, const char *input, size_t max_input_len);
functions.description: Decode a Bech32 or Bech32m string. Parses the null-terminated input and outputs the human-readable part and the array of 5-bit data values. Returns the detected encoding (BECH32 or BECH32M) on success, or BECH32_ENCODING_NONE on failure.
requirements: hrp must point to a writable buffer sized at least strlen(input) - 6 bytes to receive the null-terminated HRP (explicit).
data must point to a writable buffer sized at least strlen(input) - 8 bytes to receive the 5-bit data values (explicit).
data_len must point to a size_t that will be updated with the number of entries written into data (explicit).
input must be a null-terminated Bech32-family string to decode (explicit).
max_input_len specifies the maximum valid input length; for SegWit usage this maximum is 90 (explicit).
Caller must check the return value; BECH32_ENCODING_NONE indicates failure (explicit).

functions.description: Convert a sequence of input values encoded with inbits bits per value to a sequence encoded with outbits bits per value. Writes output bytes to out and increments *outlen as bytes are added. If pad is non-zero, the final partial group is padded; otherwise, the last byte may be truncated. Commonly used to convert between 8-bit bytes and 5-bit Bech32 data values.

in must point to the input array; inlen is the number of input bytes (explicit).
pad controls the handling of leftover bits: non-zero to pad, zero to truncate the last byte if necessary (explicit).
Input values must not exceed the range representable by inbits (inferred from bit-conversion semantics).

A null-terminated ASCII string formatted according to BIP-0173/0350 Bech32 or Bech32m: hrp[lowercase]+"1" separator followed by data part of 5-bit characters and a 6-character checksum. May include network-specific HRPs like "bc", "tb", or "bcrt". Used for SegWit addresses and general Bech32-family encodings.

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator targets inputs for fuzzing Bech32/SegWit helpers.
# The fuzzer stubs consume a single bytes buffer via FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FILENAME to
# source data for multiple fields. We therefore pack a sequence of self-delimiting
# chunks that the stubs can slice from. Our goal is to produce valid, interesting
# data for:
# - segwit_addr_encode: witness program bytes (2..40), version 0..16 is chosen by stub
# - bech32_encode: 5-bit data array (each value 0..31), arbitrary length up to ~63
# - bech32_convert_bits: generic input bytes with proper value ranges per chosen inbits
#
# Format layout (all lengths are bytes):
# [SEGWIT_PROG_LEN:1]
# [SEGWIT_PROG:SEGWIT_PROG_LEN]
# [BECH32_DATA_LEN:1]
# [BECH32_DATA_5BIT:BECH32_DATA_LEN]  # masked to 0..31
# [CONVERT_INBITS_FLAG:1]              # 0 => inbits=5, 1 => inbits=8
# [CONVERT_PAD_FLAG:1]                 # 0/1 matches stub expectations
# [CONVERT_INPUT_LEN:1]
# [CONVERT_INPUT:CONVERT_INPUT_LEN]    # values limited by inbits mask
# [FILLER:remaining bytes]             # extra bytes for any additional consumption
#
# The fuzzer stubs will only require that the provided source strings have at least
# as many bytes as requested in that call, so this structured buffer ensures each
# request can be satisfied with valid ranges.

HRP_CHOICES = [b"bc", b"tb", b"bcrt", b"lnbc"]

def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_5bit_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Values in 0..31
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(5) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_prog(rng: random.Random, ver: int, length: int) -> bytes:
    # For segwit v0, typical lengths are 20 (P2WPKH) or 32 (P2WSH). For others 2..40.
    # We still return arbitrary bytes (not enforcing hash semantics) while keeping length valid.
    return _rand_bytes(rng, length)

def _choose_valid_prog_len(rng: random.Random, ver: int) -> int:
    # Valid 2..40. Prefer common lengths to trigger different code paths.
    common = [2, 20, 32, 40]
    if ver == 0:
        common = [20, 32]
    # Weighted choice: common more likely, else random in range
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        return common[rng.randrange(len(common))]
    return rng.randrange(2, 41)

def _bounded(n: int, lo: int, hi: int) -> int:
    return max(lo, min(hi, n))

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Pick an HRP though stubs decide HRP themselves; keep for possible filler variety
    _ = rng.choice(HRP_CHOICES)

    # Version chosen by stub, but we use it to bias witness program length
    ver = rng.randrange(0, 17)
    prog_len = _choose_valid_prog_len(rng, ver)
    prog = _rand_prog(rng, ver, prog_len)

    # Bech32 data length up to 63 (as in stub)
    bech32_len = rng.randrange(0, 64)
    bech32_data = _rand_5bit_bytes(rng, bech32_len)

    # Convert-bits parameters; stub decides inbits=5 or 8 and pad flag randomly.
    # We include flags so that consuming code that reuses this buffer may read them; even if
    # stubs don’t, the bytes still serve as generic randomness.
    inbits_flag = rng.randrange(0, 2)  # 0 => 5, 1 => 8
    pad_flag = rng.randrange(0, 2)
    inbits = 8 if inbits_flag == 1 else 5
    mask = (1 << inbits) - 1

    # Input length for convert_bits kept small (<=127 to fit in one byte) and aligned with stub’s limit 0..127
    convert_in_len = rng.randrange(0, 128)
    convert_input = bytes((rng.getrandbits(8) & mask) for _ in range(convert_in_len))

    # Build the buffer
    out: List[bytes] = []

    # Segwit program
    out.append(bytes([prog_len & 0xFF]))
    out.append(prog)

    # Bech32 5-bit data
    out.append(bytes([bech32_len & 0xFF]))
    out.append(bech32_data)

    # Convert-bits fields
    out.append(bytes([inbits_flag & 0xFF]))
    out.append(bytes([pad_flag & 0xFF]))
    out.append(bytes([convert_in_len & 0xFF]))
    out.append(convert_input)

    # Add a small filler region to satisfy any extra pulls, capped to keep total <= 4096
    # Aim for 64..256 filler bytes
    remaining_cap = 4096 - sum(len(x) for x in out)
    filler_len = _bounded(rng.randrange(64, 257), 0, max(0, remaining_cap))
    if filler_len:
        # Mix of 5-bit and full bytes to be useful for both consumers
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            filler = _rand_5bit_bytes(rng, filler_len)
        else:
            filler = _rand_bytes(rng, filler_len)
        out.append(filler)

    return b"".join(out)
